title.narrative: ERW Clearance Male and Female Survey and Clearance team is recruited, trained and accredited by the Libyan Mine Action Centre to dispose of ERW in priority areas under Task Orders from the national authorities.

- Members of survey and clearance team are all accredited and accreditation certified by the Libyan Mine Action Centre. - Information Management System for Mine Action (IMSMA) reporting to the Libyan Mine Action Centre will be the indicator for results of Explosive Ordnance Disposal call-outs, unexploded ordnance destroyed and m2 of land and infra structure returned to socio-economic use.

target.value: 1b. 50,000 m2 of land/infrastructure returned to socio-economic use 1c. 100+ EOD ‘Callouts’ from the public answered 1d. 1.5 tons of Unexploded Ordnance Destroyed

actual.value: 1a. In December 2022 2 accredited humanitarian mine action teams were operating in Tripoli (1 male and 1 female). In total 12 personnel were recruited, trained and accredited. 1b. 562,327 m2 land returned to socio-economic use. 1c. 421 callouts answered and completed. 1d. 4.7 Tons of explosive ordnance marked, removed or destroyed.

target.value: 1a. 5 x personnel recruited and trained in ERW Survey & Clearance 1b. 50,000 m2 of land/infrastructure returned to socio-economic use 1c. 100+ EOD ‘Callouts’ from the public answered 1d. 1.5 tons of Unexploded Ordnance Destroyed

actual.value: 1a: By December 2021 1 accredited Multitask team was operating in Tripoli. 1b.: 294,237 m2 land returned to socio-economic use. 1c.: 206 callouts answered and completed. 1d.: 2.8 Tons of explosive ordnance marked, removed or destroyed.

title.narrative: Land and infrastructure cleared of Explosive Remnants of War (ERW) is taken-up for socio-economic use.

1a. Positive feedback from beneficiaries on Dan Church Aids (DCA) performance 1b. Quality Assurance (QA) assessments by DCA & Libyan Mine Action Centre 1c. Post-clearance impact surveys evidence increased socio-economic land use.

target.value: 100% of targeted areas of socio-economic value have been cleared of explosive remnants of war and put back into use.

actual.value: 208,050 m2 have been searched and cleared with an additional 16,864,155 m2 surveyed through NTS. Looking at the output target of 200,000 m2 (visible in the narrative report on p.4) of land returned to socio-economic use, more than 100% of the target has been reached.

title.narrative: Risk Education Risk Education team is recruited and trained, then accredited by the Libya Mine Action Centre to deliver risk awareness sessions to targeted beneficiaries under Task Orders from the national authorities.

- Members of the Risk Education team are all accredited and accreditation certified by the Libyan Mine Action Centre. - No. of Risk Education sessions conducted will be recorded - Risk Education sessions, Pre and post surveys will be conducted - Pre and post surveys will be used as a tool to change and tailor make RE sessions to the specific needs of the target group

target.value: 2a. 4 Risk Education Officers recruited and trained 2b. 55 formal Risk Education and public distribution sessions delivered 2c. 5,000 beneficiaries reached through risk education and risk awareness activities

actual.value: 2a.: 4 EORE members recruited and trained. 2b.: 339 sessions delivered (250 formal sessions and 89 public distributions). 2c. 6,834 beneficiaries (4,486 beneficiaries of formal sessions and 2,348 beneficiaries of distributions) reached through risk education and risk awareness activities.

target.value: 2b. 55 formal Risk Education and public distribution sessions delivered 2c. 5,000 beneficiaries reached through risk education and risk awareness

actual.value: 2b. 1082 sessions delivered (771 formal sessions and 311 public distributions). 2c. 29,782 beneficiaries (18,597 beneficiaries of formal sessions and 11,185 beneficiaries of distributions) reached through risk education and risk awareness activities.

title.narrative:
Psychosocial Support
Civil Society Organization is selected, trained, conducts needs assessment and delivers PSS in vulnerable communities.

- Activities and sessions with the target groups will be documented - Pre and post activity surveys will be conducted - Pre and post surveys will be used as a tool to change and to further tailor make community-based PSS sessions to the target groups and their specific needs.

target.value: 3a. 1 x CSO partner recruited and trained to implement PSS 3b. 1 x needs assessment conducted 3c. 10 x educators trained to deliver PSS activities in schools 3d. 2,500 children in vulnerable communities receive PSS

actual.value: 3a.: 1 CSO recruited and trained 3b.: 1 needs assessment conducted (see annex IV). 3c.: 9 educators trained in PSS. 3d.: 2,412 children received PSS.

target.value: 3c. 20 x educators trained to deliver PSS activities in schools 3d. 2,500 children in vulnerable communities receive PSS

actual.value: 45 educators trained in PSS and 7,284 children received PSS.

title.narrative: The wellbeing of children in vulnerable communities is increased through Community Based Psychosocial Support.
M&E in vulnerable communities record increased wellbeing amongst children

target.value: 75% of children in targeted vulnerable communities who have received psychosocial support, report increased wellbeing.

actual.value: Following the sessions, DCA conduct interviews with guardians, parents and teachers, from these interviews there was a strong indication that the PSS have contributed to the wellbeing of many boys and girls and helped to reduce negative coping mechanisms and trauma due to displacement and periods of insecurity, amongst other challenging outcomes from the conflict

title.narrative: Safety (and the adoption of safe behaviour) of the citizens of vulnerable communities is greatly increased through knowledge of dangers of mines and ERW.
2a. Mine Action Centre RE Forms show number of sessions held 2b. Mine Action Centre records show reduction in ERW related accidents 2c. Pre and Post RE session reports show increased knowledge

target.value: 75% of children, youth and adults in targeted vulnerable communities who have received explosive ordnance risk education report increased knowledge and sense of safety.

actual.value: Not visible from the narrative report.
